hook: John McCarthy earned a bachelor's degree in mathematics from Caltech in 1948 and a PhD in mathematics from Princeton in 1951. In August 1955, together with Marvin Minsky, Nathaniel Rochester and Claude Shannon, he wrote the proposal for a summer research project at Dartmouth College built on the idea that every aspect of learning or intelligence could in principle be described precisely enough for a machine to simulate it, a document that introduced the field's name. The 1956 Dartmouth workshop that followed brought together many of the researchers who would go on to define artificial intelligence as a discipline. While at MIT in 1958, McCarthy created the Lisp programming language, which became the dominant tool for AI research for decades because of its ability to manipulate symbolic expressions. He moved to Stanford University in 1962, where he founded the Stanford Artificial Intelligence Laboratory and continued developing logic based approaches to reasoning and knowledge representation until his retirement in 2000.

quick_facts: Earned a PhD in mathematics from Princeton University in 1951
Co-authored the 1955 Dartmouth proposal that introduced the term artificial intelligence
Created the Lisp programming language in 1958 while at MIT
Founded the Stanford Artificial Intelligence Laboratory after moving to Stanford in 1962
Won the ACM A.M. Turing Award in 1971 for his contributions to artificial intelligence
